privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Red News – Economic Calendar for TradingView ("the extension") displays economic-calendar news from Forex Factory on TradingView charts. It offers a free tier that works without an account, and an optional Premium tier that requires signing in. This policy explains what data the extension processes.

blocks.text: Free tier (no account): the extension does not collect names, credentials, browsing history, or advertising identifiers. It requests economic-calendar data through our own backend (see "Our backend" below); as with any network request, our backend receives your IP address in the normal course of delivering the response. We do not use this for advertising, profiling, or cross-site tracking, and we do not sell your data.
Premium tier (with account): if you choose to sign in, we collect and store:

items: your email address, name, and Google account identifier, obtained through Google sign-in, to create and identify your account and to show your name in the extension;
your subscription / entitlement status (free, trial, or premium);
a random per-installation identifier used to associate your installation with your account and to apply reasonable device limits.

blocks.text: We collect this only after you actively sign in, and only to provide the account and Premium functionality. You can stop this at any time by signing out.

Economic-calendar data and subscription checks are served by our backend hosted on Supabase (authentication, database, and server functions). The extension communicates only with our backend and with TradingView; it does not contact Forex Factory directly. Our backend fetches the public Forex Factory calendar on the server side and returns it to the extension.

items: TradingView chart pages (*.tradingview.com/chart/*): the extension reads the current chart symbol, timeframe, and timezone in order to draw the economic-news lines, labels, and tooltips on the chart. No other part of the site is accessed.
Our backend (hsoaqylcrmspyckkndab.supabase.co): the extension requests economic-calendar data and, if you are signed in, verifies your subscription status.

An AI provider of your choice (generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.groq.com or openrouter.ai): only if you connect one with your own API key, and only to request an explanation of a release you asked about. These are optional permissions — the extension has no access to any of them until you press "Connect". See AI explanations below.

blocks.text: The extension uses your browser's local storage (chrome.storage.local) to save your settings (filters, labels, alerts, timezone, language, theme), a short-lived cache of the fetched calendar data, and, if you sign in, your session tokens and account/subscription status. If you connect an AI provider, it also stores your API key and a short-lived cache of the explanations you have already received. Signing out or uninstalling removes this local data; "Remove key" removes the AI entries immediately.

If you purchase Premium, payment is processed by Paddle, which acts as the merchant of record. Your card and billing details are entered on Paddle's secure checkout and are never received or stored by us. We only receive your resulting subscription status.

With your permission, the extension shows an operating-system notification a chosen number of minutes before high-impact economic releases. Notifications are generated locally from calendar event times and are not used for messaging or marketing.

Premium users can connect a Telegram account to receive news alerts on their phone, including while their computer is off. This is entirely optional and off until you connect it. When you connect, we store on our backend your Telegram chat ID and username (supplied by Telegram when you start our bot), together with your alert preferences: impact levels, currencies, how many minutes ahead to warn you, your time zone, and any quiet hours. We use them for one purpose — deciding which alerts to send you and when — and messages are delivered through Telegram's own servers, so Telegram's privacy policy applies to their delivery. We keep a short record of which events were already sent to you so the same alert is not repeated; those records are deleted after about two days. You can disconnect at any time by blocking the bot in Telegram, and we delete the stored Telegram data when you delete your account.

sections.heading: AI explanations (optional, Premium, your own provider)

blocks.text: Premium users can connect their own AI provider — Google Gemini, Groq or OpenRouter — and press ✨ next to a release to get a plain-language briefing. This is entirely optional and does nothing until you paste your own API key. A step-by-step guide is at [rednews.app/ai](https://rednews.app/ai).

Your API key stays in your browser. It is kept in local storage on this computer, is never synchronised to other devices, and is never sent to our backend. "Remove key" deletes the key, deletes the cached answers, and withdraws the extension's permission to contact the provider.
Requests go straight from your browser to the provider you chose. They do not pass through our servers. We cannot see what you asked or what the model answered.

What is sent: the scheduled release itself — title, currency, impact level, scheduled time in UTC, and its forecast, previous and actual values — up to six earlier prints of that same release taken from the extension's own calendar history, and the language the answer should be written in. Your API key travels in the request's authorisation header, as the provider requires. Nothing else is included: no name or email, no account or subscription details, no chart symbol, no browsing history, and no text you type.

The provider's own privacy policy governs what it does with that request. Providers differ: some state that they do not retain or train on API traffic by default, while others may use free-tier traffic to improve their products. The current position of each supported provider is summarised on the setup page, but you should read your provider's own terms.
Answers are cached locally for up to seven days (at most sixty of them) so that reopening the same event does not spend your quota again. The cache never leaves your browser.

Access is granted per provider, at the moment you connect. The three provider addresses are optional permissions: Chrome asks for your consent when you press "Connect", and until then the extension cannot reach any of them.

If you send feedback through the extension ("Report a problem, idea, or partnership"), the message you type, an optional email address, and basic non-personal context (the extension version, your browser, and your interface language) are sent through Web3Forms, a third-party form-delivery service, which forwards them to the developer by email. This happens only when you press Send.

items: Supabase hosts our backend (authentication, database, server functions) that serves calendar data and stores your account/subscription status.
Google provides the sign-in through which we obtain your name, email, and account identifier.
Paddle processes Premium payments as merchant of record; card data never reaches us.
Forex Factory is the source of the public economic-calendar data, fetched by our backend.
Web3Forms delivers feedback you choose to send.
Telegram delivers the optional Premium alerts to users who connect our bot.

Google (Gemini API), Groq, OpenRouter are AI providers a Premium user may connect with their own API key. We hold no account or contract with them on your behalf; your browser talks to whichever one you chose, directly, and only for the explanations you request.

blocks.text: Each third party processes data subject to its own privacy policy.

The free tier works without an account. If you have signed in, you can sign out at any time, and you may request deletion of your account data by contacting us (see "Contact"). Deleting your account removes your stored email, name, account identifier, and subscription record.
Any change that affects what data is collected or how it is processed will be reflected in an updated Privacy Policy before it takes effect. The "Last updated" date above will be revised.

For questions about this policy or to request account deletion, email [support@rednews.app](mailto:support@rednews.app?subject=Red%20News%3A%20Privacy%20question) or reach us on [Discord](https://discord.com/users/1172891214580830322).

refund.title: Refund Policy
refund.intro: We want you to be happy with Red News Premium. This policy explains how trials, cancellations, and refunds work. Payments are processed by Paddle, our merchant of record, so refunds are issued through Paddle to your original payment method.

blocks.text: Every new user can start a 14-day Premium trial with no payment method required. The trial is long enough to span a major economic release, so you can fully evaluate Premium before you are ever charged. We encourage you to use it.
If you subscribe and change your mind, you can request a full refund within 14 days of your first payment, no questions asked. This applies to the initial charge on a monthly or annual plan.

Subscriptions renew automatically. To avoid a renewal charge, cancel before your renewal date using the Manage subscription button in the extension. After cancellation you keep Premium until the end of the period you have already paid for. Renewal charges are generally non-refundable, but if you were charged for a renewal you did not intend to keep and reach out promptly, contact us. We review these case by case and aim to be fair.

items: Reply to the Paddle receipt email you received for the purchase, or
email [support@rednews.app](mailto:support@rednews.app?subject=Red%20News%3A%20Refund%20request) with the email address used at checkout, or
reach us on [Discord](https://discord.com/users/1172891214580830322).

blocks.text: Approved refunds are processed by Paddle back to your original payment method, typically within 5 to 10 business days depending on your bank or card provider.
Nothing in this policy limits any refund or cancellation rights you may have under the consumer-protection laws of your country of residence, or under Paddle's own buyer terms as merchant of record.
